name: Elvis Clark

bio.statement: Ballotpedia records that Elvis Clark, a Republican, ran for the Oregon House in District 41 in 2024.
bio.excerpt: Elvis Clark (Republican Party) ran for election to the Oregon House of Representatives to represent District 41.

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists Clark's occupation as retired economist, with a background as Senior Economist at the Oregon Utility Commission.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Retired Economist Occupational Background: Senior Economist, Oregon Utility Commission

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 50

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists a master's degree from Portland State as his educational background.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 50

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists the Milwaukie Public Safety Committee (2018-2026) as his prior governmental experience.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Milwaukie Public Safety Committee (2018-2026)

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 50

positions.statement: Ballotpedia lists U.S. Term Limits among pledges Clark signed in 2024.
In his pamphlet statement, Clark says he wants to hold the line against taxes and regulations, and argues that scaling back low-benefit state programs would remove the need for new taxes.
positions.excerpt: Eliminating or dialing back these programs would eliminate the need to create new taxes.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 50

positions.statement: Clark says in his pamphlet statement that the state Clean Fuels program adds about $200 million in gasoline costs for Oregonians and is a red-tape burden on the economy.
positions.excerpt: There is the state's "Clean" Fuels program costing Oregonians $200 million in higher gasoline costs

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 50

positions.statement: Clark's pamphlet statement criticizes the state for taking on over $500 million in debt to add urban renewal costs to the Rose Quarter I-5 project.
positions.excerpt: going in hock for over $500 million - adding urban renewal costs onto the cost of the Rose Quarter I-5 project.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 50

positions.statement: Clark says in his pamphlet statement that the state should stop creating new programs funded by one-time federal money, which he says leads to new state taxes and fees.
positions.excerpt: The state government creates new programs with one-time federal monies, creating new government dependencies, causing state government to gin up new taxes and fees.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 50

positions.statement: On his campaign site, Clark supports requiring voter approval of new city taxes and fees, pointing to an Ashland measure and asking for the same in Milwaukie.
positions.excerpt: How about the same Measure for Milwaukie?
